title: La boda
desc: Your own wedding, and forty people with opinions
setting: Two weeks out. Doña Elena has the list, Lucía has the dress, and somebody has to say something about the money.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Van a ser como ciento veinte personas.
steps.en: It is going to be about a hundred and twenty people.

options.es: Ciento veinte. ¿Y quiénes son los padrinos?
options.en: A hundred and twenty. And who are the godparents?
options.feedback: You did not flinch at the number and you went straight to who is paying for what. That is the real question.

options.en: A hundred and twenty? That is a lot.
options.feedback: Honest. It also sounds like the first move in an argument about cutting the list.

options.es: Nosotros no conocemos a tanta gente.
options.en: We do not know that many people.
options.feedback: You do not. Her family does, and the wedding belongs to more people than the two of you.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Hay padrino de pastel, de música y de las sillas.
steps.en: There is a godparent of the cake, of the music and of the chairs.

options.es: Ah, entonces no lo paga una sola familia.
options.en: Ah, so one family does not pay for it all.
options.feedback: You understood the whole system in one sentence. That is the answer she was waiting to hear.
True, and it treats the padrinos as a discount rather than as people.

options.en: I would rather pay for it all myself.
options.feedback: It sounds generous and it is an insult. You would be shutting her family out of their own wedding.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: A usted le toca hablar con el padre.
steps.en: It falls to you to talk to the priest.

options.es: Va. ¿Qué es lo que tengo que llevar?
options.en: Right. What do I need to take?
options.feedback: Accepted the job and asked for the list. Nothing else was needed.
Because it is yours. Asking why turns a task into a negotiation.

options.es: Que vaya Lucía, ella lo conoce.
options.en: Let Lucía go, she knows him.
options.feedback: She does. The point is that the priest meets the man.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y no se me ponga nervioso el día.
steps.en: And do not go getting nervous on me on the day.

options.es: Nervioso voy a estar, doña. Pero ahí voy a estar.
options.en: I will be nervous, doña. But I will be there.
options.feedback: Admitted the first half and promised the second. That is exactly the right size of answer.
Reassuring and empty. She was not really asking about nerves.
In two weeks, in front of a hundred and twenty people, that will not survive contact.
